contributions.statement: In production harnesses LSP is a post-write diagnostics channel, not a retrieval index: OpenCode appends diagnostics from ~25 auto-downloaded language servers to every edit result, and Hermes uses LSP only after writes. Retrieval stays ripgrep/glob/tree-sitter. A JDT-LS integration for Java fits the host as an edit-feedback sensor more naturally than as a search tool.
contributions.evidence: §13.2 Table 13 rows for OpenCode and Hermes; §6 loop notes (OpenCode feeds LSP diagnostics into edit results).

contributions.statement: No pinned production coding harness (0/11) retrieves source code with embeddings; embeddings appear only for conversation memory. Any host the team adopts will not supply code RAG, so adding it is a team-owned component with its own staleness cost.
contributions.evidence: §13.2 Absence 2, manifest and import sweep repeated across twelve trees three months apart.

contributions.statement: Before adding semantic code retrieval, show it beats ripgrep plus tree-sitter on a held-out task set.
contributions.evidence: §16 Rec. 16; the paper itself runs no such comparison.

reason: The inventory gives a dated, verifiable fact a Java team can act on: hosts ship lexical retrieval and treat LSP as diagnostics feedback, so a JDT-LS MCP belongs on the edit-feedback path. The 'no code RAG' advice is adoption-based. Its effectiveness side is contested by measured KB evidence (2607.25431), so it does not count as new.
